title: AI-written books on Amazon squeeze human authors out of the market
excerpt: Anthropic's AI training using millions of used books raised copyright concerns. The market impact of AI-generated content is a key issue.
content_html:
Evidence of unfair use: AI books squeeze human authors out of the market

By Alistair Barr

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Author of the Tech Memo newsletter

Of all the things Anthropic has done, this one probably shocks regular people the most. The AI giant bought millions of used books, cut off their spines, scanned the contents to train its models, and then destroyed the originals.

Most people hear that and think it's awful. But Anthropic was actually following copyright law, which lets you digitize a book you own as long as you don't create an extra copy. In a high-profile case, a federal judge ruled this part of Anthropic's process was fair use.

The bigger question has always been what happens after the training, when models use what they've learned to generate new content.

The US Copyright Office examined that issue last year and identified the biggest weakness in AI companies' argument. One of the four fair-use tests asks whether the new work harms the market for the original. The Copyright Office concluded that using copyrighted works to create commercial content that competes with those works "goes beyond traditional fair-use boundaries."

The problem was proving it. Now there's evidence.

Researchers recently analyzed more than 14,000 ebooks sold on Amazon between 2023 and 2026. They found many books with substantial amounts of AI-written text — so many that they squeezed the market for everyone else.

The number of books with sales exploded 19-fold, while the total amount of money readers spent on those books grew ninefold. In other words, the market got much more crowded without growing nearly as fast, leaving less revenue for the average title. Books with no detected AI text lost market share as AI books spread, the researchers also found.

That's exactly the kind of market harm the Copyright Office said courts should be looking for. When AI can produce thousands of books at almost no cost, human authors end up competing against a flood of new content (that wouldn't exist without their original work).

Ed Newton-Rex, CEO of the nonprofit Fairly Trained, noted that AI companies have said their models don't financially harm the creators whose work they learned from. This research leaves that argument "well and truly dead," he wrote on X.

不公平使用的证据：人工智能书籍将人类作者挤出市场

作者：Alistair Barr 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。 《技术备忘录》时事通讯的作者

在 Anthropic 所做的所有事情中，这件事可能是最让普通人震惊的。 这家人工智能巨头购买了数百万本旧书，切掉书脊，扫描内容来训练模型，然后销毁原版。

大多数人听到这句话并认为这很糟糕。 但 Anthropic 实际上遵循版权法，只要您不创建额外的副本，就可以将您拥有的书籍数字化。 在一个备受瞩目的案件中，一位联邦法官裁定 Anthropic 程序的这一部分属于合理使用。

更大的问题始终是训练后，当模型使用他们学到的知识来生成新内容时会发生什么。

美国版权局去年审查了这个问题，并发现了人工智能公司论点的最大弱点。 四项合理使用测试之一询问新作品是否损害原作市场。 版权局的结论是，使用受版权保护的作品来创建与这些作品竞争的商业内容“超出了传统的合理使用界限”。

问题在于证明这一点。 现在有证据了。

研究人员最近分析了 2023 年至 2026 年间在亚马逊上销售的 14,000 多本电子书。 他们发现许多书籍都有大量人工智能编写的文本——数量如此之多，以至于他们挤占了其他人的市场。

销量的书籍数量猛增了 19 倍，而读者在这些书籍上花费的总金额则增长了 9 倍。 换句话说，市场变得更加拥挤，但增长速度却没有那么快，导致普通游戏的收入减少。 研究人员还发现，随着人工智能书籍的传播，没有检测到人工智能文本的书籍失去了市场份额。

这正是版权局表示法院应该寻找的市场损害。 当人工智能几乎可以免费生产数千本书时，人类作者最终会与大量新内容竞争（如果没有他们的原创作品，这些内容就不会存在）。

非营利组织 Fairly Trained 的首席执行官埃德·牛顿-雷克斯 (Ed Newton-Rex) 指出，人工智能公司表示，他们的模型不会在经济上损害他们从中学习的创作者。 他在 X 上写道，这项研究让这一论点“彻底消亡”。
